function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools, platforms, and APIs you can use to book flights—whether you’re building a travel app, automating a booking workflow, or just looking for the best way to find and reserve seats.

| Category | Tool / Service | What it does | Typical Use‑Case |
|----------|----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Search & book flights, hotels, car rentals, packages. | General consumer bookings. |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregates flight prices from many airlines & OTAs. | Price comparison. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global flight search, price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | Flexible travel planning. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” map. | Quick price checks & route ideas. |
| | **Momondo** | Aggregates fares, shows price trends. | Price‑sensitive travelers. |
| | **Priceline** | Includes “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals. | Last‑minute deals. |
| | **Orbitz** | Similar to Expedia, often bundled with hotel rewards. | Loyalty program integration. |
| | **Travelocity** | OTA with a focus on package deals. | Family vacations. |
| | **CheapOair** | Focus on low‑fare flights, often with promo codes. | Budget travelers. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” deals for flights & hotels. | Surprise‑price savings. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels, but offers flight booking in some regions. | One‑stop booking. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia, offers flights, hotels, trains. | International travel. |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** | Not flights, but sometimes includes local flight booking. | Experiential travel. |
| | **Agoda** | Hotels & flights in Asia. | Asian market focus. |
| | **Ctrip / Trip.com** | Chinese OTA, strong airline partnerships. | China‑centric travel. |
| | **Traveloka** | Southeast Asia OTA, includes flights. | SEA market. |
| | **MakeMyTrip** | Indian OTA, flights & packages. | India market. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA, flights & packages. | EU market. |
| | **TUI** | European OTA, flights & holiday packages. | All‑in‑one holiday. |
| | **eDreams** | European OTA, flights & hotels. | Budget travel. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Last‑minute flight & package deals. | Urgent bookings. |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregator, also offers price alerts. | Price monitoring. |
| | **FlightHub** | Focus on Asia‑Pacific flights. | Regional deals. |
| | **CheapTickets** | Low‑fare flights, often with promo codes. | Budget travelers. |
| | **JetRadar** | Aggregates flight prices, price alerts. | Price comparison. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Deals & coupons for flights & hotels. | Deal hunters. |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network for flight bookings. | Monetization. |
| | **Skiplagged** | Hidden‑city ticketing, price hacks. | Advanced travelers. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for discounted fares. | Price alerts. |
| | **Hopper** | Predictive pricing, tells you when to book. | Timing optimization. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” map. | Quick price checks & route ideas. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight status & tracking. | Real‑time flight info. |

### Quick‑Start API Picks

| API | Key Features | Where to Get It |
|-----|--------------|-----------------|
| **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Full flight search, booking, seat selection, ancillary services. | https://developers.amadeus.com |
| **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive flight inventory, booking, and airline data. | https://developer.sabre.com |
| **Travelport APIs** | Flight, hotel, car, and package booking. | https://developer.travelport.com |
| **Skyscanner API** | Search & price alerts, multi‑city itineraries. | https://partners.skyscanner.net |
| **Google Flights API (via Google Cloud)** | Flight search, price history, seat availability. | https://cloud.google.com/ |
| **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, historical data. | https://flightaware.com/commercial/api |
| **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data, open source. | https://opensky-network.org |
| **AviationStack API** | Flight status, schedules, airports. | https://aviationstack.com |
| **FlightStats API** | Flight status, delays, historical data. | https://developer.flightstats.com |
| **Airline APIs (e.g., Delta, United, Lufthansa)** | Direct booking, seat selection, loyalty integration. | Airline developer portals |

### How to Build a Flight‑Booking Flow

1. **Search** – Use Amadeus, Sabre, or Skyscanner APIs to pull flight options.
2. **Select** – Present options to the user; let them choose flight, cabin, seat.
3. **Book** – Call the airline or GDS API to create a reservation.  
   *If you’re using a GDS (Sabre/Travelport), you’ll need a GDS account and credentials.*
4. **Payment** – Integrate a payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree).  
   *Many GDS APIs handle payment, but you can also use a third‑party processor.*
5. **Confirmation** – Receive a PNR/confirmation number, send e‑ticket via email or SMS.
6. **Post‑Booking** – Offer seat upgrades, add-ons, or loyalty points.

### Tips for Choosing the Right Tool

| Need | Recommended Tool |
|------|------------------|
| Cheapest fares | Skyscanner, Kayak, Google Flights |
| Full booking & seat selection | Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport |
| Real‑time flight status | FlightAware, OpenSky, AviationStack |
| Multi‑city itineraries | Amadeus, Skyscanner |
| Loyalty program integration | Airline APIs (e.g., Delta, United) |
| Rapid prototyping | Skyscanner, Google Flights |
| Enterprise‑grade solution | Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus |
